summary: The lecture covers Fundamental Duties under Part 4A of the Indian Constitution, added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Sardar Swaran Singh Committee, borrowing from the Soviet Constitution. Originally 10 duties were listed under Article 51A; an 11th duty regarding education for children aged 6-14 was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002. The lecture details all 11 duties and mentions the next topic will be Part 5 (Central Government).
points: 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added Fundamental Duties via new Part 4A and Article 51A on Swaran Singh Committee recommendation.
Fundamental Duties borrowed from the erstwhile Soviet Union (Russia) Constitution.
Originally 10 Fundamental Duties; 11th added by 86th Amendment Act, 2002 as Article 51A(k).
Article 51A(a): Duty to respect Constitution, its ideals, institutions, National Flag and National Anthem.
Article 51A(c): Duty to uphold and protect sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.
Article 51A(d): Duty to defend the country and render national service when called upon.
Article 51A(e): Duty to promote harmony, common brotherhood, renounce practices derogatory to women.
Article 51A(g): Duty to protect and improve natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife.
Article 51A(h): Duty to develop scientific temper, humanism, spirit of inquiry and reform.
Article 51A(k): Duty of parents/guardians to provide education opportunities for children aged 6-14 years.
